thread:
jordan.m: alert: sudden spike in origin QPS after last deploy, KV prefix cache hit-rate dropped from ~85% to ~12%. paging eng-sre, looks like cache stampede.

li-chen: which cache? prefix/prompt cache on runtime-kv service? any traces?

jordan.m: yes runtime-kv. Grafana panels attached (snippet):
```
cache.prefix.hit_rate: 85% -> 12% (09:08 -> 09:11)
runtime-kv.origin_qps: 1200 -> 5400
runtime-kv.origin_5xx: 0.4% -> 2.5%
requests.lat_p50: 45ms -> 180ms
```

anya: who deployed last? I see a canary at 08:52. Deploy-bot?\
deploy-bot: canary deploy of runtime-server v2.14.3 (commit 7f3b2c) started 2024-04-04T08:52:17Z by mike_r

mike_r: that was me, small change in cache key construction to attempt deduping of dynamic prompt metadata. I added request.headers.x-session to key builder.

li-chen: that rings alarm bells — including ephemeral header will explode cardinality. Can we toggle prefix caching off quickly?

jordan.m: starting feature-flag toggle now:
```
# flip prefix cache off
curl -X POST "$CONSOLE/api/flags/runtime.prefix_cache_enabled" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"value":false}'
{"status":"ok","flag":"runtime.prefix_cache_enabled","value":false}
```

sre-bot: alert_ack: incident-ch1 assigned to oncall (anya).

anya: good. Monitoring shows origin QPS stabilizing but still high. We need immediate mitigation + root cause.

li-chen: quick triage: confirm cache key change. Dumped git diff around key builder:
```
- key = join([model, prefix_hash])
+ key = join([model, prefix_hash, request.headers['x-session']])
```
That adds session id — terrible.

mike_r: I pushed that to reduce cross-user collisions for some internal experiment. My bad. Rolling back now or patch to strip ephemeral parts and keep stable identifiers?

jordan.m: rollback is faster. Initiating rollback of v2.14.3 -> v2.14.2 on canary and then rollout.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for runtime-server canary -> v2.14.2 (commit 4b8e1a)

mike_r: rolling back complete. Observability shows hit_rate climbing: 12% -> 67% in 7 minutes. Origin QPS trending down.

li-chen: rollback avoided catastrophic overload but we still see cold-cache thrash leading to origin load. Need warmup and better keying rules plus guardrails. Suggestions:
- normalize cache keys to drop ephemeral headers by default
- add automated cardinality monitor on key entropy with alert at >1e6 unique keys/min
- add fast fail toggle that disables prefix caching per-customer on overload
- implement throttled origin fallback: token-bucket when cache miss QPS spikes

anya: agree. For immediate follow-ups: ticket for keying revert + unit tests, telemetry alert for key cardinality, and a warming job to re-populate cache after recoveries. I'll create tasks.

mike_r: small patch ready to normalize key:
```
- raw_session = request.headers.get('x-session')
- key_parts.append(raw_session)
+ session = request.headers.get('x-session')
+ session = None if session and session.startswith('tmp-') else session
+ # only include known stable session types
+ if session:
+   key_parts.append(session)
```
This drops tmp-* sessions and prevents high-cardinality inclusion.

li-chen: also add hash bucketing on long fields: `hash(field) % 1000` to reduce cardinality explosion if needed.

jordan.m: warming job proposal: simple kinesis-driven replay that issues top-50k prefixes we saw last 24h at a controlled rate: 50rps for 20 minutes. Script preview:
```
for p in top_prefixes:
  curl -X POST $RUNTIME/gen -d '{"model":"x","prompt":p}'
  sleep 0.02
```
I'll run in staging first.

anya: run warmup in prod in a throttled window and monitor origin load. Also add a rolling disable if origin CPU > 70% for > 2m.

jordan.m: warmup started 10:05 UTC (throttled). Initial result: hit_rate -> 75% after 18 minutes, origin QPS back near baseline.

sre-bot: incident severity downgraded.

li-chen: for postmortem items:
- cause: inadvertent inclusion of ephemeral header in cache key (commit 7f3b2c)
- immediate mitigation: feature-flag toggle + rollback to v2.14.2
- follow-ups: key normalization PR, cardinality alerts, warmup tooling, automated feature flag on overload, add unit tests verifying key stability across ephemeral headers

mike_r: opening PR for key normalization and tests now: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/482

anya: assigning tasks to eng-runtime and eng-sre. Will schedule 30m post-incident review at 14:00 UTC.

jordan.m: note — we also saw a secondary regression: the kernel selection path was doing extra KV lookups per token for a short path that assumed cache hits. When misses spiked it increased per-request GPU work. Filed perf follow-up to avoid redundant KV accesses on cache miss fast-path.

li-chen: good catch. Add that to the perf backlog.

mike_r: sorry again for the regression. Learned: never include free-form headers in cache keys.

anya: closing thread after follow-ups created. We should capture the warmup script as a runbook item. :white_check_mark:
